Drummer Terri Lyne Carrington was born into a musical family in Boston on August 4, 1965. She has performed and recorded with a diverse list of artists, including Herbie Hancock, James Moody and Robin Eubanks. Terri was the house drummer on both “The Arsenio Hall Show” and “Vibe.” Her first album as a leader is entitled “Jazz is a Spirit.”
Terri was interviewed in Toronto, Canada on January 9, 2003 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Toronto for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have Terri Lyne Carrington with me this morning.
Welcome. Quite a scene here at the IAJE, isn’t it?

Yeah, it’s always quite a scene, I mean you never know who you’re going to run into, especially depending on what city it’s in. Last year it was in Los Angeles and so I was able to go most of the days because I live in that area, and it was amazing how many people you see at these events, that you don’t run into just maybe once a year at something like this or a lot of times you run into people at the North Sea Jazz Festival in the summer. But IAJE has a way of really bringing people together. I know a lot of people just come to hang out at this point that aren’t performing, I mean musicians. I know Kenny Barron came this year and Ndugu Chancler, and I don’t think they’re performing they just came.
That’s really great. And people get to meet and greet, especially the people that live on one coast might not see the New York people etcetera.
